chunks: And Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the one sentenced to stoning who flees.
He said: "If he confessed to himself, he is not returned; and if witnesses testified against him, he is returned."
And it has been narrated: "If the pain of the stones had struck him, he is not returned; and if the pain of the stones had not struck him, he is returned."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person sentenced to stoning who flees before the punishment is completed?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the conditions for halting the execution of stoning (rajm) based on the mode of proof, distinguishing between voluntary confession and witness testimony. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where the certainty of guilt via witnesses necessitates completion of the penalty, whereas a confessor's status may allow for discretion. The alternative narration further refines this by linking the finality of the punishment to the physical experience of the penalty, emphasizing the principle of proportionality in judicial execution.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5020 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a person sentenced to stoning who attempts to flee.
Imam (as) replied: "If the person confessed to the crime himself, he should not be brought back. However, if witnesses testified against him, he must be returned."

It has also been narrated: "If the person had already been struck and felt the pain of the stones, he should not be brought back. But if he had not yet felt the pain of the stones, he should be returned."
